The RV32I opcode listing shows LB and LBU as distinct load instructions with different funct3 values. It gives no extension semantics, so it is only auxiliary.

grades.quote: The LW instruction loads a 32-bit value from memory and sign-extends this to 64 bits before storing it in register _rd_ for RV64I. The LWU instruction, on the other hand, zero-extends the 32-bit value from memory for RV64I. LH and LHU are defined analogously for 16-bit values, as are LB and LBU for 8-bit values.
grades.reason: It explains that signed loads sign-extend and the unsigned variants zero-extend to the register width. It says LB/LBU are defined analogously to LW/LWU, so LB sign-extends the byte (a high bit of 1 gives upper bits of 1) and LBU zero-extends it.
